newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Anderton, Clark meet to discuss coalition.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Anderton, Clark meet to discuss coalition.

text.p: Alliance leader Jim Anderton said on Tuesday he had already met Labour leader Helen Clark to discuss working together in a coalition government and further talks were planned.
Anderton announced important changes in his party's strategy on Sunday, saying it was ready to go into coalition with Labour after the next election without a detailed agreement before the vote.
Last year the parties were at odds because the Alliance said it would not negotiate a coalition after the election and Labour refused to make a deal before it.
Anderton said the Alliance had been right to adopt that stance last year because it was the first MMP election, but things had changed.
"We have time to work through some of the problems. I've met Helen Clark, we've worked through some of the things and we've agreed to meet again," he told National Radio.
"That means we've got a mechanism to get some clarification, and a process by which we negotiate. We've got time to do it," he said. -- Wellington Newsroom (64-4-4734746)
